rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body; this is a narrative closer, not an interactive demo beat.
All six chunks carry multi-paragraph, self-carrying content; none is a bare wait-state or a single context-dependent bullet.

Each ## header matches its chunk's content: 'Wrong is how steering gets in' (wrongness becomes rules), 'The rules started doing the work' (rules become load-bearing across sessions), 'Then the agents started checking the agents' (subagent + parallel-agent audit fan-out), 'Built to forgive' (missing artifacts cost only a file), 'You just ran the compound loop' (direct address confirming the reader just ran it). None contradicted by its own chunk.

Not-X-Not-Y-Z: only one 'Not'-led sentence exists in the body (chunk 1, 'Not wrong the way a bad draft is wrong... Wrong the way any first version is wrong...'), a single negation-then-assertion, not the banned two-negations-plus-Z shape. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: chunk 1's 'Some were overscoped. Some went off in the wrong passage. Some held for one kind of content and broke for another' repeats 'Some' three times, but the third leg carries new concrete content (content-type dependence vs. the first two legs' scope/placement issues) -- passes the third-leg test; chunk 3's one-person to subagent to four-agents-plus-a-fifth escalation likewise adds new content on every leg. Self-grading superlatives: none found -- 'the valuable part' (chunk 1) grades the narrative gap, not the training's own worth. Number + retraction: none -- 'ninety minutes, not a year' / 'a trivial bug, not a whole training' (chunk 5) is a scale contrast between two real durations, not a hedge-then-walk-back of one figure. Abstraction-noun stacks: 'work-per-session' / 'care-per-line' (chunk 3) are cashed out concretely in the same breath ('a week got made in an afternoon'). Verb triplets with an empty leg: none -- 'saw the wrongness, named it, corrected it' and 'used, corrected, rewritten' are each three concrete verbs.
